# bytedance/protenixsparkPowered by Gemini

# bytedance/protenixsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 8, 2026Commit[`c3bfc36`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/tree/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix predicts biomolecular structures, generating atomic\-level models for proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules\. It operates as an open\-source framework, providing tools for computational biology research, data preparation, model training, and performance evaluation\.

 Protenix's primary function is biomolecular structure prediction\. It allows generation of models from input sequences and features, with prediction tasks initiated via a command\-line interface that processes standardized JSON inputs\. The system employs a diffusion process to iteratively refine atomic positions, guided by an internal [protenix\.py L91](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/protenix.py#L91) model\. [Setting Up and Running Protenix](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix) and [Protenix Model Architecture and Training](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-model-architecture-and-training) describe these processes further\.

 The framework focuses on computational efficiency\. It incorporates custom kernel implementations for operations like Layer Normalization and attention mechanisms, and utilizes techniques such as shared variable caching, efficient kernel fusion, and TF32 acceleration\. These methods improve the speed and efficiency of the prediction pipeline\. [Performance Optimization Techniques](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#introduction-to-protenix-biomolecular-structure-prediction-performance-optimization-techniques) provides details on these specific techniques\.

 Protenix enhances structure predictions through Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\)\. This engine refines the model's sampling process without requiring additional training, applying configurable energy\-based potentials to enforce geometric and chemical constraints on atomic coordinates\. TFG steers predictions toward physically realistic and chemically sound structures\. [Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#training-free-guidance-tfg) describes this functionality\.

 A range of pre\-trained model variants are available, balancing accuracy with computational requirements\. These include models optimized for specific use cases, such as incorporating experimental constraints or leveraging protein language model embeddings\. All models undergo benchmarking against diverse datasets, evaluating performance against established baselines and other methods\. [Model Variants and Benchmarking](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#introduction-to-protenix-biomolecular-structure-prediction-model-variants-and-benchmarking) outlines these models and their evaluation\.

 Protenix handles comprehensive biological data management and preparation\. This includes downloading and processing structural and sequence data from external databases like PDB, Rfam, and RNAcentral\. It converts raw mmCIF files into structured [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) objects, generates Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSA\), and prepares template features for model input\. [Data Management and Preparation for Protenix](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix) details these processes\.

 The framework integrates concepts from other projects, notably AlphaFold3, and uses external bioinformatics tools for essential preprocessing steps\. These tools include [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10) for MSA generation and [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209) or [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370) for template and RNA MSA searches\. This integration ensures robust data preparation for accurate predictions\. [Integration with Related Projects](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#introduction-to-protenix-biomolecular-structure-prediction-integration-with-related-projects) covers these external dependencies\.

 A centralized configuration system manages settings for the machine learning pipeline, covering run parameters, data processing, model architecture, and inference specifics\. This system handles default values, type enforcement, and command\-line argument overrides\. [Configuration Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#configuration-management) explains the system in depth\.

 Protenix offers web service functionalities for computational biology inference, supporting web\-based applications\. These services process requests, manage data downloads, perform MSA searches using systems like MMseqs2, and provide visualization tools for prediction results\. Interactive Jupyter widgets facilitate the definition of complex molecular inputs\. [Protenix Web Services](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-web-services) describes these capabilities\.## Introduction to Protenix: Biomolecular Structure Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix is an open\-source framework designed for high\-accuracy biomolecular structure prediction, serving as a research tool for computational biology\. It provides accessible and extensible tools for structural prediction, building upon concepts from projects like AlphaFold3\. Its mission and scope encompass robust structure prediction, continuous performance optimization, flexible model variants, comprehensive benchmarking, and seamless integration with other computational biology tools\.

 The core capability of Protenix is its biomolecular structure prediction\. Users can predict structures via a command\-line interface, [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L1), which processes JSON inputs and utilizes specified models\. The central [protenix\.py L91](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/protenix.py#L91) class, defined in [`protenix/model/protenix.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/protenix.py), orchestrates various components including feature embedding, [pairformer\.py L227](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/modules/pairformer.py#L227), [diffusion\.py L231](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/modules/diffusion.py#L231), and confidence heads to execute the [protenix\.py L306](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/protenix.py#L306) process for prediction\. Inference workflows are managed by the [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) class within [`runner/inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py), handling environment setup, model initialization, checkpoint loading, and result dumping\. See [Managing Inference Workflows with InferenceRunner](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-managing-inference-workflows-with-inferencerunner) for more details\.

 Performance optimization is a key focus for Protenix\. Recent versions, such as [README\.md?plain=1 L35](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L35), introduced advanced diffusion inference optimizations like shared variable caching, efficient kernel fusion, and TF32 acceleration\. The framework also incorporates custom kernel setups for specific operations, such as [layer\_norm\.py L190](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/layer_norm/layer_norm.py#L190) implemented using custom CUDA kernels within [`protenix/model/layer_norm`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/layer_norm), and Triton\-optimized [op\.py L167](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention/op.py#L167) mechanisms found in [`protenix/model/tri_attention`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention)\. These optimizations are critical for enhancing the speed and efficiency of the prediction process\. For a deeper dive into performance aspects, refer to [Optimized Layer Normalization with CUDA Kernels](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-model-architecture-and-training-optimized-layer-normalization-with-cuda-kernels) and [Triton\-Optimized Tri\-Attention Mechanism](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-model-architecture-and-training-triton-optimized-tri-attention-mechanism)\.

 Protenix offers a diverse range of model variants, each tailored for different use cases and computational requirements\. These include "Base Models" for high accuracy, "Mini & Tiny Models" designed for efficiency, a "Constraint Model" that incorporates experimental constraints, "ESM & ISM Models" leveraging ESM2\-3B embeddings, and "Protenix\-v2" which represents an enhanced capacity model\. These models are extensively benchmarked against various datasets to evaluate their performance against baselines and other state\-of\-the\-art methods, such as AlphaFold3\. The documentation in [`docs`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs) provides detailed benchmark results for different Protenix versions\.

 Beyond its core prediction capabilities, Protenix incorporates Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\) to refine structural predictions without requiring additional training\. The TFG engine, located in [`protenix/tfg`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg), allows configurable potentials, such as [potentials\.py L1134](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L1134) and [potentials\.py L594](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L594), to steer the diffusion sampling process, leading to improved structural accuracy\. More information can be found in [Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#training-free-guidance-tfg)\.

 Protenix also integrates with and builds upon concepts from other projects, such as AlphaFold3\. It leverages external tools for essential preprocessing steps, including [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10) for Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) generation and [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209) and [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370) for template generation and RNA MSA searches, respectively\. These integrations are facilitated by scripts within [`scripts`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts) and runner modules in [`runner`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner), ensuring comprehensive data preparation for accurate predictions\.### Performance Optimization Techniques

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix optimizes its performance through a combination of custom kernel setups, shared variable caching, and efficient kernel fusion, which collectively enhance the speed and efficiency of biomolecular structure prediction\. TF32 acceleration further contributes to this by leveraging specialized hardware capabilities\.

 A key technique for performance optimization involves custom CUDA\-accelerated Layer Normalization, implemented in [`protenix/model/layer_norm`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/layer_norm)\. This [layer\_norm\.py L190](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/layer_norm/layer_norm.py#L190) module offloads computations to specialized CUDA kernels, which are dynamically compiled or imported\. The kernels, located in [`protenix/model/layer_norm/kernel`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/layer_norm/kernel), perform both forward and backward passes using techniques like Welford's algorithm for numerical stability, warp\-level reductions for parallel efficiency, and vectorized memory access\. This approach aims to provide a 30\-50% speedup over native PyTorch implementations\. Users can opt for the native PyTorch Layer Normalization by setting the [train\_demo\.sh L15](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/train_demo.sh#L15) environment variable to [\.flake8 L31](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/.flake8#L31), as described in [`docs/kernels.md`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/kernels.md)\.

 Another critical optimization is the "Tri\-Attention" mechanism, primarily implemented using NVIDIA's Triton framework for high\-performance scaled dot\-product attention\. The [op\.py L167](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention/op.py#L167) module in [`protenix/model/tri_attention`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention) leverages Triton kernels for its forward and backward passes\. These kernels utilize block pointers for efficient memory access and are designed for tiled processing and fused operations\. To ensure broad compatibility, Protenix includes a PyTorch fallback implementation for environments where Triton is unavailable or unsupported, routing the attention calculation to [primitives\.py L248](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/modules/primitives.py#L248)\. Triton's [forward\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention/forward.py#L22) decorator is used with predefined configurations in [`protenix/model/tri_attention/autotune_helpers.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention/autotune_helpers.py) to optimize kernel launch parameters for different hardware and input shapes at runtime\. Furthermore, the [autotune\.py L41](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention/autotune.py#L41) class in [`protenix/model/tri_attention/autotune.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/tri_attention/autotune.py) extends Triton's autotuning capabilities by persisting optimal kernel configurations to disk\. This caching mechanism reduces redundant autotuning across multiple runs or process restarts, leading to faster startup times and improved efficiency\. Protenix also supports other triangle attention implementations, including those from [kernels\.md?plain=1 L20](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/kernels.md?plain=1#L20) and [kernels\.md?plain=1 L23](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/kernels.md?plain=1#L23), configurable via [kernels\.md?plain=1 L11](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/kernels.md?plain=1#L11), as detailed in [`docs/kernels.md`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/kernels.md)\.

 Beyond these custom kernels, Protenix incorporates efficient kernel fusion and shared variable caching, though specific file paths for these generalized techniques are not explicitly detailed in the provided summaries\. The framework's overall design, including the use of optimized components and dynamic compilation of kernels, underscores a strong focus on maximizing computational efficiency\. This is particularly relevant given the resource\-intensive nature of biomolecular structure prediction, where performance directly impacts throughput and research capabilities\.### Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\) for Structure Refinement

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix employs a Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\) engine to refine biomolecular structure predictions during the diffusion sampling process without requiring additional model training\. This engine is designed to enforce geometric and chemical constraints on atomic coordinates, thereby steering the generative model towards more physically realistic and chemically sound structures\. The TFG framework in Protenix is modular, allowing for the configuration and application of various potential energy terms\.

 At the core of the TFG system is the [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) class, located in [`protenix/tfg/engine.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py)\. This engine orchestrates the application of guidance, refinement, and projection steps within the model's [protenix\.py L306](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/protenix.py#L306) algorithm\. It integrates configured TFG terms, which are defined through a flexible configuration system described in [`protenix/tfg/config.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py)\. This system allows users to specify time\-varying schedules for parameters, such as guidance weights, using constructs like [config\.py L61](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L61) and [config\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L72) schedules\. Each potential energy term is encapsulated in a [config\.py L188](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L188) object, which defines its evaluation interval, weight schedule, and potential\-specific parameters\.

 The TFG engine utilizes a range of differentiable potentials, implemented in [`protenix/tfg/potentials.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py), to calculate energy penalties and their corresponding gradients with respect to atomic coordinates\. These potentials include:

 - **[potentials\.py L594](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L594)**: Manages distance constraints between atom pairs, incorporating Van der Waals radii and providing mechanisms for feasibility repair through coordinate projection\.
- **[potentials\.py L849](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L849)**: Enforces the correct chirality of chiral centers in molecules\.
- **[potentials\.py L984](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L984)**: Applies planarity constraints to specific atomic groups, often found in sp2 hybridized systems\.
- **[potentials\.py L1134](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L1134)**: Implements a Vina\-style empirical steric potential, particularly useful for modeling inter\-chain contacts and avoiding clashes between molecules by identifying candidate collision pairs and applying a penalty based on distance\.

 During the [protenix\.py L306](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/model/protenix.py#L306) process, the [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) dynamically applies these potentials\. It can guide the denoising process by computing gradients of the energy function and shifting the noisy coordinates towards regions of lower energy, or by directly refining the predicted noise\-free coordinates through iterative gradient ascent on the log probability \(or gradient descent on energy\)\. The engine also supports iterative projection steps to enforce hard constraints or local refinements, ensuring that the generated structures adhere to specified geometric and chemical rules\. This modular and configurable approach enables fine\-grained control over the structural properties of predicted biomolecules\.### Model Variants and Benchmarking

| Model Name Pattern | Size/Type | Key Features | Use Case / Trade\-offs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| protenix\_base\_default\_v0\.5\.0 | Base | Standard model, N\_cycle: 10, sample\_diffusion\.N\_step: 200 | High accuracy, scientific research |
| protenix\_base\_constraint\_v0\.5\.0 | Base | Constraint support \(pocket, contact embedders\) | Predictions with structural priors |
| protenix\-v2 | Base \(Enhanced\) | Increased representation dimensionality \(c\_z=256\), N\_cycle: 10, sample\_diffusion\.N\_step: 200 | Richer representations, improved fidelity |
| protenix\_mini\_default\_v0\.5\.0 | Mini | Lightweight, N\_cycle: 4, sample\_diffusion\.N\_step: 5 | Efficient, good balance of speed & accuracy |
| protenix\_mini\_esm\_v0\.5\.0 | Mini | ESM2\-3B embeddings, no MSA by default | Better performance when MSAs unavailable |
| protenix\_mini\_ism\_v0\.5\.0 | Mini | ISM embeddings, no MSA by default | Better performance when MSAs unavailable |
| protenix\_tiny\_default\_v0\.5\.0 | Tiny | Minimal, N\_cycle: 4, sample\_diffusion\.N\_step: 5 | Maximum efficiency, high\-throughput screening |

Protenix offers a range of pre\-trained model variants, each designed to balance prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and specific application needs\. These models are categorized by their size, the features they leverage, and their version number, following a [supported\_models\.md?plain=1 L8](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/supported_models.md?plain=1#L8) naming convention, as detailed in [`docs/supported_models.md`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/supported_models.md)\.

 The core [README\.md?plain=1 L71](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L71) represent the full\-parameter versions, optimized for the highest prediction accuracy\. For scenarios requiring faster inference or operating within resource\-constrained environments, [README\.md?plain=1 L37](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L37) and [supported\_models\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/supported_models.md?plain=1#L1) are available\. These variants achieve efficiency by reducing network blocks and the number of diffusion steps, offering a trade\-off between speed and accuracy\.

 Specialized model variants address particular structural prediction challenges\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L62) \([supported\_models\.md?plain=1 L46](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/supported_models.md?plain=1#L46)\) integrates experimental structural constraints, such as contact and pocket definitions, to guide predictions with prior knowledge\. For improved performance when Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) are unavailable, [inference\_demo\.sh L41](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/inference_demo.sh#L41) incorporate embeddings from protein language models like ESM2\-3B\. [README\.md?plain=1 L82](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L82) represents an advanced iteration of the base model, featuring increased representation dimensionality and an expanded parameter space for enhanced modeling fidelity in complex tasks\.

 The performance of these models undergoes rigorous evaluation through an extensive benchmarking framework\. Protenix models are assessed against various datasets, including [model\_0\.5\.0\_benchmark\.md?plain=1 L17](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/model_0.5.0_benchmark.md?plain=1#L17), [model\_0\.5\.0\_benchmark\.md?plain=1 L17](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/model_0.5.0_benchmark.md?plain=1#L17), [model\_0\.5\.0\_benchmark\.md?plain=1 L17](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/model_0.5.0_benchmark.md?plain=1#L17), and a [parser\.py L2188](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/parser.py#L2188) set, adhering to the AlphaFold3 inference protocol\. This involves generating multiple predictions per target \(e\.g\., 25 predictions from 5 model seeds and 5 diffusion samples\) and ranking them by confidence scores\.

 Benchmark results, such as those for [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L1) and [README\.md?plain=1 L1](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/README.md?plain=1#L1), are documented in [`docs/model_0.5.0_benchmark.md`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/model_0.5.0_benchmark.md) and [`docs/model_1.0.0_benchmark.md`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/model_1.0.0_benchmark.md), respectively\. These documents provide detailed performance metrics, comparisons against other models, and access to the datasets used for evaluation\. Downloadable benchmark packages include inference metrics in CSV format and aggregated results, facilitating in\-depth analysis of model performance across diverse molecular structures and prediction scenarios\.### Integration with Related Projects

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix integrates with other projects by building upon concepts from systems like AlphaFold3 and leveraging external bioinformatics tools to enhance its biomolecular structure prediction capabilities\. The system incorporates external search tools to gather essential data for its models\. For instance, for protein Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\), Protenix utilizes [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10), orchestrating its execution and processing the resulting A3M files\. This is managed by the [colabfold\_msa\.py L41](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py#L41) within [`scripts/colabfold_msa.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py), which is responsible for parsing and splitting A3M content, particularly for multimer inputs\. The execution of [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10) is handled by [colabfold\_msa\.py L191](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py#L191), as detailed in [`scripts/colabfold_msa.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py)\.

 For template searches, Protenix relies on [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209) and [search\.py L141](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L141), which are HMMer tools used to search against sequence databases\. The [template\_search\.py L45](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py#L45) function, found in [`runner/template_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py), manages this process, including locating binaries and downloading the necessary sequence databases\. Similarly, RNA MSA searches are performed using [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370), a tool from the HMMer suite, against specialized databases such as Rfam and RNAcentral\. The [rna\_msa\_search\.py L178](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/rna_msa_search.py#L178) function in [`runner/rna_msa_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/rna_msa_search.py) coordinates these searches, handling database downloads and merging results\.

 The integration of these external search tools is crucial for preparing the comprehensive input data required for Protenix's inference pipeline\. The [batch\_inference\.py L589](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L589) \([`runner/batch_inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py)\) serves as the primary command\-line interface, providing subcommands like [batch\_inference\.py L1081](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1081), [batch\_inference\.py L1160](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1160), and [batch\_inference\.py L1288](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1288) to orchestrate these searches and update the inference JSONs with the generated MSA and template information\. This layered approach allows Protenix to benefit from established bioinformatics methods while focusing its core development on advanced modeling and prediction\. For more details on the command\-line interface, refer to [Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Protenix Operations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-command-line-interface-cli-for-protenix-operations)\.## Setting Up and Running Protenix

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix provides a command\-line interface \(CLI\) to manage its operations, enabling users to perform structure prediction, convert data formats, and execute sequence and template searches\. The primary executable is accessed via the [batch\_inference\.py L589](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L589) command, which is defined in [`runner/batch_inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py)\. This CLI orchestrates various tasks through subcommands, offering a streamlined workflow for biomolecular structure prediction\.

 The [inference\.py L204](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L204) subcommand initiates the full inference pipeline, which includes preprocessing steps and model prediction\. For tasks like converting PDB/CIF and ligand files into Protenix's required JSON input format, the [batch\_inference\.py L986](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L986) subcommand is used\. The system also supports [batch\_inference\.py L1081](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1081), [batch\_inference\.py L1160](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1160), and [batch\_inference\.py L1288](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1288) subcommands to handle Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) searches, template searches, and a combination of both, respectively\. These preprocessing steps are crucial for preparing biological data for the prediction model\.

 The core of the inference process is managed by the [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) class, located in [`runner/inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py)\. This class handles the environment setup, model initialization, checkpoint loading, and the execution of prediction workflows\. It ensures that necessary data caches and model weights are downloaded and that model configurations are updated for GPU compatibility\. After predictions are generated, the [dumper\.py L48](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L48) class, found in [`runner/dumper.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py), manages the persistence of results\. This includes saving structural coordinates in CIF format and storing confidence data in JSON files, with options for ranking predictions based on quality\.

 Beyond protein MSA, Protenix also supports RNA MSA searches using [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370), as detailed in [`runner/rna_msa_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/rna_msa_search.py)\. This capability allows for generating alignments against databases like Rfam and RNAcentral\. Similarly, template searches, facilitated by [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209) and [search\.py L141](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L141), identify structural templates from databases to aid in protein structure prediction\. This process is managed by [template\_search\.py L45](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py#L45) and [template\_search\.py L159](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py#L159) in [`runner/template_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py)\. The overall inference workflow is designed to be robust, incorporating error handling and logging to ensure reliability\. For a deeper understanding of how the CLI operates and its various subcommands, refer to [Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Protenix Operations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-command-line-interface-cli-for-protenix-operations)\. To learn how [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) orchestrates prediction tasks, see [Managing Inference Workflows with InferenceRunner](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-managing-inference-workflows-with-inferencerunner)\. For details on how results are stored, consult [Data Persistence and Result Dumping](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-data-persistence-and-result-dumping), and for MSA and template search specifics, refer to [Performing MSA and Template Searches](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-performing-msa-and-template-searches)\.### Command\-Line Interface \(CLI\) for Protenix Operations

| Command | Description | Preprocessing Steps Included |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pred | Runs inference for structure prediction based on input JSON files\. | MSA search, template search, and RNA MSA search \(if enabled\)\. |
| json | Converts PDB or CIF files into the JSON format required for Protenix inference\. | Input file conversion \(PDB to CIF if needed\)\. |
| msa | Performs MSA \(Multiple Sequence Alignment\) search using MMseqs2 for protein sequences\. | None \(only performs MSA search\)\. |
| mt | Conducts MSA search followed by template search\. | MSA search and template search\. |
| prep | Executes a complete preprocessing pipeline: MSA search, template search, and RNA MSA search\. | MSA search, template search, and RNA MSA search\. |

The [batch\_inference\.py L589](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L589) provides a command\-line interface for interacting with the Protenix system, allowing users to perform various tasks related to biomolecular structure prediction, data conversion, and preprocessing\. This CLI, defined in [`runner/batch_inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py), orchestrates the entire inference pipeline, manages data preparation, and facilitates the use of external tools for sequence and template searching\.

 The core commands available through [batch\_inference\.py L589](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L589) are:

 - **[inference\.py L204](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L204)**: This command initiates the full inference pipeline\. It configures the model, prepares input data by performing necessary preprocessing steps like Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) and template searches, and then executes the structure prediction\. It supports batch processing of multiple input JSON files\. Further details on the inference workflow can be found in [Managing Inference Workflows with InferenceRunner](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-managing-inference-workflows-with-inferencerunner)\.
- **[batch\_inference\.py L986](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L986)**: This utility converts common structural biology file formats, specifically PDB and CIF files, into the standardized JSON input format required by Protenix models\. This facilitates the preparation of diverse structural data for prediction tasks\.
- **[batch\_inference\.py L1081](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1081)**: This command performs Multiple Sequence Alignment searches\. It can either update an existing inference JSON file with MSA results or perform a standalone MSA search on a FASTA file\. The process of generating and processing MSA data is further elaborated in [Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) Data Generation and Featurization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix-multiple-sequence-alignment-msa-data-generation-and-featurization)\.
- **[batch\_inference\.py L1160](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1160)**: This command combines the functionalities of MSA and template searching\. It takes a JSON input file, performs both types of searches, and updates the JSON with the results\. More information on template data processing can be found in [Template Data Processing and Featurization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix-template-data-processing-and-featurization)\.
- **[batch\_inference\.py L1288](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L1288)**: This command provides a comprehensive preprocessing step, performing MSA, template, and RNA MSA searches sequentially on a given JSON input file\. This ensures all necessary input features are generated before a prediction task\. Details on RNA MSA searches are available in [Performing MSA and Template Searches](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix-performing-msa-and-template-searches)\.

 The CLI uses the [batch\_inference\.py L26](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L26) library for robust command\-line argument parsing and subcommand management, and it relies on configuration files and external binaries for various tasks, such as [kalign\.py L27](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/kalign.py#L27), [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209), and [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370)\. The overall configuration management within Protenix is described in [Configuration Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#configuration-management)\.### Managing Inference Workflows with InferenceRunner

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) class, defined in [`runner/inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py), serves as the central orchestrator for executing prediction workflows within Protenix\. It manages the lifecycle of an inference task, from initial setup to result output\.

 Upon instantiation, the [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) initializes the execution environment, configuring distributed processing and CUDA devices to leverage available hardware resources efficiently\. It also sets up output directories for storing prediction results and logging potential errors\. The runner then loads the Protenix model and its associated weights from a specified checkpoint, ensuring the model is ready for inference\. This includes handling checkpoint formats for distributed data parallel \(DDP\) setups by adjusting key prefixes\.

 A key responsibility of the [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) is managing the download of necessary data caches and model checkpoints\. This ensures that all required external resources, such as chemical component dictionaries or pre\-trained ESM models, are available before predictions commence\.

 During the prediction phase, the [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) iterates through input data, dynamically adjusting model configurations based on the size of the input sequence to optimize memory usage and prevent out\-of\-memory errors\. It then executes the model's forward pass, performing predictions, and subsequently uses a data dumper to save the structural coordinates, confidence metrics, and other relevant outputs\. This process includes error handling and logging to ensure robust operation\. Furthermore, [inference\.py L64](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L64) ensures GPU compatibility by modifying configurations for specific hardware architectures, such as older GPUs that might require different data types or kernel implementations for stable operation\.### Data Persistence and Result Dumping

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [dumper\.py L48](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L48) class, defined in [`runner/dumper.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py), manages the persistence of biomolecular structure prediction results\. It organizes and saves the output of Protenix models, including both the predicted structural coordinates and associated confidence scores\.

 When a prediction is made, [dumper\.py L48](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L48) creates a structured directory system to store the results, typically organized by dataset, PDB ID, and a unique seed\. It then orchestrates the saving of two primary types of data:

 1. **Structural Coordinates:** The predicted 3D structures are saved in CIF \(Crystallographic Information File\) format\. This involves taking an [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) object, which represents the molecular structure, and converting it into a CIF file\. Optionally, predicted per\-atom confidence scores \(pLDDT\) can be incorporated into the CIF file as B\-factor values, providing a visual indication of local model confidence when structures are viewed in molecular visualization software\.
2. **Confidence Data:** Various confidence metrics and detailed prediction data are stored in JSON format\. This includes summary confidence scores \(e\.g\., global pLDDT, PAE\), and can optionally include more detailed atom\-level confidence information\. Before saving, numerical values in the confidence data are typically rounded for cleaner output\.

 To help users identify the best predictions, the [dumper\.py L48](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L48) can rank the output samples based on a specified [dumper\.py L227](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L227) extracted from the summary confidence data\. If ranking is enabled, the output files are named in a way that reflects their quality, making it easier to select the most promising models\.### Performing MSA and Template Searches

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix performs Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) searches and template searches as critical preprocessing steps for biomolecular structure prediction\. These processes involve generating sequence alignments and identifying homologous structural templates, which enrich the input data for the prediction models\.

 For general protein sequences, the [msa\_search\.py L125](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L125) function within [`runner/msa_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py) orchestrates the MSA generation\. This process checks if an MSA search is needed, converting older MSA data formats if necessary, and then executes the search\. It generates results for each protein sequence and updates the task's JSON data with paths to the newly created paired and unpaired MSA files\. This ensures that the downstream prediction pipeline has access to comprehensive sequence alignment information\.

 For RNA sequences, a specialized [batch\_inference\.py L50](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/batch_inference.py#L50) process, detailed in [`runner/rna_msa_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/rna_msa_search.py), is employed\. This function utilizes [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370) to perform parallel searches against multiple RNA\-specific databases such as NT\-RNA, Rfam, and RNAcentral\. It manages the download of these databases, configures the [search\.py L370](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L370) tool, and merges the results into a single A3M\-formatted MSA\. The [rna\_msa\_search\.py L379](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/rna_msa_search.py#L379) function then integrates these RNA MSA paths into the inference JSON data\.

 Template searches are conducted by the [template\_search\.py L45](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py#L45) function in [`runner/template_search.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py), primarily using [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209) and [search\.py L141](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L141)\. This process searches against a sequence database to find structural templates\. It ensures the availability of the necessary binaries and manages the download of the [msa\_template\_pipeline\.md?plain=1 L111](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/msa_template_pipeline.md?plain=1#L111) database if it's not present locally\. The function takes existing MSA files, concatenates them, and executes [search\.py L209](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tools/search.py#L209) to generate [infer\_json\_format\.md?plain=1 L56](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/infer_json_format.md?plain=1#L56) files containing the template information\. The [template\_search\.py L159](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/template_search.py#L159) function integrates these template paths into the inference JSON, ensuring that structural prediction models can leverage known homologous structures\.

 These preprocessing steps are crucial for preparing the diverse biological data required by the Protenix models\. For more details on the overall pipeline, refer to [Setting Up and Running Protenix](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#setting-up-and-running-protenix) and [Data Management and Preparation for Protenix](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix)\. The [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) in [`protenix/web_service`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service) also utilizes these MSA search capabilities as part of its web service request processing, as described in [Web Service Request Processing and Inference Orchestration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-web-services-web-service-request-processing-and-inference-orchestration)\.## Data Management and Preparation for Protenix

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix employs a robust data management and preparation system to handle diverse biological data essential for biomolecular structure prediction\. This system encompasses the download, processing, and organization of sequence and structural data from various external databases, alongside the preparation of training data and Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) data\.

 For external data sourcing, Protenix utilizes scripts to download and process data from the Protein Data Bank \(PDB\), such as filtering the [template\_parser\.py L44](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py#L44) file to retain only protein entries via [`scripts/database/generate_pdb_seqres.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/database/generate_pdb_seqres.py)\. RNA\-centric data is managed through scripts that download and cluster [rna\_msa\_search\.py L128](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/rna_msa_search.py#L128) active sequences using [msa\_search\.py L129](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L129), as seen in [`scripts/database/generate_rnacentral_cluster_file.sh`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/database/generate_rnacentral_cluster_file.sh)\. Similarly, Rfam data is downloaded, merged, and clustered for RNA analysis using [msa\_search\.py L129](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L129) by [`scripts/database/generate_rfam_cluster_file.sh`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/database/generate_rfam_cluster_file.sh)\. The overall download and extraction of Protenix\-specific datasets, including both inference\-only and full datasets, is orchestrated by [`scripts/database/download_protenix_data.sh`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/database/download_protenix_data.sh)\.

 The preparation of training data from mmCIF files involves a series of steps to extract biological assemblies and generate sample indices\. The script [`scripts/prepare_training_data.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/prepare_training_data.py) processes individual mmCIF files, extracts bioassembly information, and saves it, along with compiling sample indices into a CSV file\. This process leverages parallel execution to efficiently handle large datasets\.

 Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) data is a critical input for many prediction tasks\. The system extracts protein and nucleic acid sequences from mmCIF files, generating FASTA and JSON outputs as detailed in [`scripts/msa/step1-get_prot_seq.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step1-get_prot_seq.py)\. MSA data from [colabfold\_msa\.py L220](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py#L220) files is enriched by incorporating NCBI TaxIDs into UniRef headers, a process managed by [`scripts/msa/step3-uniref_add_taxid.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step3-uniref_add_taxid.py)\. Furthermore, MSA files are split based on sequence type \(UniRef100 versus other sequences\) into distinct files, as demonstrated in [`scripts/msa/step4-split_msa_to_uniref_and_others.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step4-split_msa_to_uniref_and_others.py)\. The [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10) tool is integrated for generating MSAs, with a dedicated script [`scripts/colabfold_msa.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py) for managing its execution and processing the resulting [colabfold\_msa\.py L220](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py#L220) files, including handling multimer inputs\. The data management components within Protenix ensure that raw biological data is transformed into a structured and readily usable format for downstream machine learning models\.### Core Structural Data Processing and Featurization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix processes and prepares biomolecular structure data, starting from parsing mmCIF files into structured [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) objects\. This involves extracting a structure, handling alternate locations, and generating biological assemblies from symmetry operations\. The [parser\.py L93](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/parser.py#L93) in [`protenix/data/core/parser.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/parser.py) is responsible for these tasks, creating an [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) from mmCIF data and then applying a series of filtering and annotation steps through methods like [parser\.py L445](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/parser.py#L445) and [parser\.py L692](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/parser.py#L692)\. This pipeline includes [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) cleaning operations such as removing water, hydrogens, short polymer chains, and resolving clashes between chains, which are managed by the [filter\.py L28](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py#L28) class in [`protenix/data/core/filter.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py)\.

 Once the structural data is parsed and cleaned, it is converted into numerical features and labels suitable for machine learning models\. The [featurizer\.py L29](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/featurizer.py#L29) class in [`protenix/data/core/featurizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/featurizer.py) handles this transformation, generating token\-level features, reference features, bond features, and masks\. This includes creating local coordinate frames for tokens using methods like [featurizer\.py L236](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/featurizer.py#L236), which relies on [featurizer\.py L145](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/featurizer.py#L145) for biopolymers and [featurizer\.py L178](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/featurizer.py#L178) for ligands\. Additionally, the [tokenizer\.py L104](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L104) in [`protenix/data/tokenizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py) converts [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) objects into [tokenizer\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L22) and [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) objects, where each token can represent a residue or an atom, facilitating the featurization process\.

 The system also integrates information from the Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) through [`protenix/data/core/ccd.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/ccd.py) to provide detailed reference information and manage inter\-residue bonds\. Furthermore, [substructure\_perms\.py L208](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/substructure_perms.py#L208) in [`protenix/data/core/substructure_perms.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/substructure_perms.py) generates permutations of atom indices, accounting for molecular symmetry and stereochemistry, which is used in the [geometry\_featurizer\.py L101](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/geometry_featurizer.py#L101) within [`protenix/data/core/geometry_featurizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/geometry_featurizer.py) to extract geometry and stereochemistry features from reference chemical descriptions\. This comprehensive processing ensures that the structural data is accurately represented and prepared for downstream machine learning tasks\.### Preparing Training Data and Biological Assemblies

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The Protenix system prepares training data from mmCIF files by orchestrating a sequence of processing steps to extract, filter, and organize structural and biological assembly information\. This pipeline is managed primarily through the [data\_pipeline\.py L44](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/pipeline/data_pipeline.py#L44) class in [`protenix/data/pipeline/data_pipeline.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/pipeline/data_pipeline.py), which is responsible for parsing raw mmCIF data, tokenizing structural components into a [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62), and featurizing various aspects such as Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSA\) and templates\.

 The process begins by using [prepare\_training\_data\.py L52](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/prepare_training_data.py#L52) to parse individual mmCIF files\. This function extracts biological assembly information, generates indices for sampling, annotates the [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) \(the fundamental representation of atomic structures\) with resolution details, and converts it into a [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62)\. The [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) represents the structure at a higher level of abstraction, suitable for machine learning models\.

 A significant part of this preparation involves extensive filtering and annotation, drawing on utilities within [`protenix/data/core/filter.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py)\. These steps refine the [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) to ensure data quality and relevance for model training\. For example, methods within this module remove water molecules, hydrogens, and other unwanted elements\. They also handle ambiguities in residue types and manage alternate conformations\. Critical filtering steps address the complexity of biological assemblies by:

 - Removing short or broken polymer chains\.
- Applying [filter\.py L175](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py#L175) to select representative subsets of chains when an assembly exceeds a predefined maximum chain count, often prioritizing core interacting components\.
- Performing [filter\.py L368](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py#L368) to eliminate chains that exhibit high clash ratios, a process guided by an iterative clash detection algorithm similar to those used in established structure prediction methods\.
- Correcting for [filter\.py L584](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py#L584) to address instances where covalent bonds across polymers or between polymers and ligands might be inconsistently represented across symmetric copies of a complex\.
- Using [filter\.py L842](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/filter.py#L842) to consistently select alternate conformations based on occupancy, ensuring a unified representation across multi\-residue blocks\.

 After initial parsing and filtering, the pipeline integrates Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) information through [ccd\.py L222](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/ccd.py#L222) in [`protenix/data/core/ccd.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/ccd.py), which provides reference features for non\-standard residues and ligands\. This information is crucial for generating accurate geometric and stereochemical constraints\. The [geometry\_featurizer\.py L101](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/geometry_featurizer.py#L101) in [`protenix/data/core/geometry_featurizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/geometry_featurizer.py) then extracts these geometry and stereochemistry constraints, aligning RDKit\-derived features with the BioTite atom indices and handling molecular symmetry to avoid over\-constraining symmetric parts of a molecule\.

 The output of this comprehensive preparation is stored in a structured format\. For each processed mmCIF file, a gzipped pickle file containing the [utils\.py L437](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/utils.py#L437) is saved, and [parser\.py L1903](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/core/parser.py#L1903) are compiled into a CSV file\. This enables efficient loading for model training, as described in [Preparing Training Data and Biological Assemblies](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix-preparing-training-data-and-biological-assemblies)\. The [prepare\_training\_data\.py L29](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/prepare_training_data.py#L29) and [prepare\_training\_data\.py L63](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/prepare_training_data.py#L63) functions in [`scripts/prepare_training_data.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/prepare_training_data.py) orchestrate this process, including parallel execution to handle large datasets effectively\.### Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) Data Generation and Featurization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) data generation and processing in Protenix involves a series of steps designed to prepare sequence information for use in biomolecular structure prediction models\. This workflow extracts sequences, performs homology searches, enriches alignment data with taxonomic information, and organizes these alignments into structured features\.

 The initial step involves extracting protein and nucleic acid sequences from mmCIF files\. This process is handled by scripts like [`scripts/msa/step1-get_prot_seq.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step1-get_prot_seq.py), which parses individual mmCIF files, identifies polymeric entities, and extracts their one\-letter code sequences\. The script organizes this information into DataFrames, generates FASTA files for protein sequences, and creates JSON mappings that link unique sequences to PDB entity IDs and integer identifiers\. This integer indexing helps manage sequences efficiently in subsequent steps\.

 After initial sequence extraction, the system performs homology searches to generate MSAs\. This can involve tools like [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10), orchestrated by scripts such as [`scripts/colabfold_msa.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py)\. This script executes [colabfold\_compatible\_msa\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/colabfold_compatible_msa.md?plain=1#L10) and then processes the resulting A3M files\. For multimer predictions, it specifically handles the splitting of A3M content into pairing and non\-pairing sequences for individual chains\. HMMER searches are also supported for generating template alignments [Integration with Related Projects](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#introduction-to-protenix-biomolecular-structure-prediction-integration-with-related-projects)\.

 A subsequent refinement step involves enriching the generated A3M files with NCBI TaxIDs\. The [`scripts/msa/step3-uniref_add_taxid.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step3-uniref_add_taxid.py) script reads mappings between UniRef IDs and NCBI TaxIDs from an [step2\-get\_msa\.ipynb L1](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step2-get_msa.ipynb#L1) file\. It then modifies the headers of UniRef entries in A3M files to include the corresponding TaxIDs\. This process leverages multiprocessing and optimized binary file reading to handle large datasets efficiently\.

 Further processing of MSAs involves splitting them based on sequence type\. The [`scripts/msa/step4-split_msa_to_uniref_and_others.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/msa/step4-split_msa_to_uniref_and_others.py) script divides A3M files into separate categories: one for UniRef100 sequences and another for all other sequences\. The output is organized into subdirectories named after a PDB index, facilitating structured storage\. This script also uses parallel processing and can utilize shared memory for large mapping datasets to optimize performance\.

 Once MSA data is generated and processed, it undergoes featurization to prepare it for machine learning models\. The [`protenix/data/msa`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa) directory contains classes such as [msa\_featurizer\.py L369](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa/msa_featurizer.py#L369) and [msa\_featurizer\.py L579](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa/msa_featurizer.py#L579), which manage the conversion of raw MSA data into numerical features\. The [msa\_featurizer\.py L42](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa/msa_featurizer.py#L42) retrieves raw MSA content, and the [msa\_featurizer\.py L161](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa/msa_featurizer.py#L161) transforms it into a structured [msa\_featurizer\.py L527](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa/msa_featurizer.py#L527) object\. This transformation includes pairing protein chains based on species identifiers using the [msa\_utils\.py L262](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/msa/msa_utils.py#L262), filtering gapped rows, and merging features across different chains\. This ensures that the MSA data is properly formatted and includes context relevant to multiple interacting molecular entities\. The process ensures that both training and inference workflows can efficiently access and utilize MSA data\.### Template Data Processing and Featurization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Handling protein template data in Protenix involves a multi\-stage process of parsing, filtering, and featurizing\. This process transforms raw template search results into a standardized format suitable for model input\.

 The [template\_featurizer\.py L216](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py#L216) class in [`protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py) coordinates the template featurization workflow\. It manages the configuration and distinguishes between training and evaluation phases, applying template dropout during training and caching results for efficiency\. It retrieves and parses templates, then processes biological assemblies to generate features\.

 Parsing of various template formats is handled by the [template\_parser\.py L233](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py#L233) in [`protenix/data/template/template_parser.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py)\. This component interprets mmCIF files for structural information and [template\_parser\.py L584](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py#L584) and [template\_parser\.py L656](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py#L656) for parsing HHR and A3M files, respectively, extracting alignment statistics and sequences into [template\_parser\.py L550](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py#L550) objects\.

 Template hits undergo filtering and detailed processing through components in [`protenix/data/template/template_utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_utils.py)\. The [template\_utils\.py L313](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_utils.py#L313) screens [template\_parser\.py L550](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_parser.py#L550) objects based on criteria such as release date, alignment ratio, and sequence length\. The [template\_utils\.py L384](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_utils.py#L384) extracts atomic coordinates and re\-aligns query sequences to hit sequences, generating feature dictionaries\. The [template\_utils\.py L759](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_utils.py#L759) integrates these steps, processing multiple template hits and supporting the ingestion of JSON templates\.

 The [template\_featurizer\.py L111](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py#L111) in [`protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py) assembles the processed template features\. It standardizes feature representation and ensures consistent tensor shapes, padding features to a maximum limit\. The [template\_featurizer\.py L553](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py#L553) dataclass holds core template features and provides methods to compute advanced features such as pseudo\-beta masks, distograms, and unit vectors from atomic positions\.

 For inference scenarios, the [template\_featurizer\.py L662](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py#L662) in [`protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/template/template_featurizer.py) provides a simplified interface for template featurization, reusing the assembly line for efficient processing\. This modular approach supports the integration of template information into the overall data pipeline [Data Management and Preparation for Protenix](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix)\.### Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) Cache Management

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)
