The system identifies two types of clashes: those based on AlphaFold3 \(AF3\) principles and those based on Van der Waals \(VDW\) radii\. These are quantified by measuring distances between atoms and comparing them against defined thresholds\. The process distinguishes between various chain types such as protein, DNA, RNA, and ligand, and can skip clash calculations for potentially bonded ligand\-polymer pairs to avoid false positives, as detailed in [`protenix/metrics/clash.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/metrics/clash.py)\.

 LDDT scores provide a measure of local structural similarity, assessing how well a predicted structure matches a reference at the atomic level\. Protenix calculates complex\-level, chain\-level, and interface\-level LDDT metrics\. These scores can be aggregated using various strategies, including selecting the best, worst, mean, median, or a random sample, as well as rank\-based aggregation according to confidence scores such as pLDDT or gpde\. The system optimizes memory usage during LDDT calculations for large atomic systems by employing a sparse distance computation approach\. Further details are available in [`protenix/metrics/lddt_metrics.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/metrics/lddt_metrics.py)\.

 RMSD is used for calculating the global structural deviation between predicted and true molecular poses, and for aligning structures\. Protenix implements functionalities for standard RMSD calculation, as well as methods to align a predicted structure to a reference using an optimal rigid body transformation derived from the Kabsch algorithm\. This alignment can be performed considering specific atoms or weights, and the system can also calculate RMSD for partially aligned or self\-aligned structures\. These alignment and deviation calculations are central to comparing predicted models with experimental or reference structures, and are implemented in [`protenix/metrics/rmsd.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/metrics/rmsd.py)\.## Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\)

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\) in Protenix enhances the biomolecular structure prediction process by steering the model's diffusion sampling without requiring additional training of the core prediction model\. This is achieved through the application of energy\-based potentials that enforce geometric and chemical constraints on atomic coordinates\.

 The system is designed with a modular architecture, with its primary components found in the directory [`protenix/tfg`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg)\. Configuration of TFG is handled by [`protenix/tfg/config.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py), which allows for user\-defined settings to be converted into structured runtime objects\. This includes defining time\-varying schedules, which determine how parameters evolve over the diffusion process\. For example, a [config\.py L40](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L40) \(defined in [`protenix/tfg/config.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py)\) can specify how the weight of a particular constraint changes from the beginning to the end of the sampling process\.

 A [config\.py L188](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L188) object \(also defined in [`protenix/tfg/config.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py)\) encapsulates a single TFG energy potential, including its evaluation interval, a weight schedule, and any potential\-specific parameters\. These terms can calculate an energy, an energy gradient, or apply coordinate projections\.

 The core runtime logic for applying TFG during diffusion sampling is managed by the [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) class, located in [`protenix/tfg/engine.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py)\. This engine orchestrates the integration of guidance, refinement, and projection steps into the sampling process\. It can compute the total energy and its gradient from active TFG terms, estimate the log\-probability of the denoised structure using Monte Carlo samples, and iteratively refine predicted structures\.

 Various differentiable potentials, defined in [`protenix/tfg/potentials.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py), form the basis of TFG's ability to enforce constraints\. These potentials include mechanisms to manage pairwise distances \([potentials\.py L594](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L594)\), ensure chirality \([potentials\.py L849](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L849)\), enforce planarity \([potentials\.py L984](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L984)\), or apply Vina\-style steric terms \([potentials\.py L1134](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L1134)\)\. Each potential can compute an energy penalty for violations, as well as providing gradients to guide coordinates towards desired configurations or suggesting coordinate updates for projection\-like operations\. These mechanisms collectively allow TFG to guide the diffusion model towards structurally plausible and chemically sound predictions\.### Core TFG Engine and Sampling Integration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) is central to integrating Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\) into Protenix's diffusion sampling process\. Located in [`protenix/tfg/engine.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py), this engine orchestrates the application of configurable TFG potentials, which act as soft constraints to steer the biomolecular structure generation\.

 During a diffusion step, the [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) guides the process through several mechanisms\. First, it applies denoiser\-path guidance, controlled by the [config\.py L380](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L380) parameter\. This involves calculating the log probability of the predicted initial coordinates \([engine\.py L395](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L395)\) based on the TFG potentials and then using the gradient of this log probability to subtly shift the noisy coordinates \([engine\.py L25](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L25)\) before the primary denoise operation\. This guides the diffusion path towards states favored by the defined potentials\.

 Next, the engine incorporates projection steps\. These steps iteratively refine the predicted initial coordinates \([engine\.py L450](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L450)\) by applying specific coordinate updates derived from TFG terms that implement a projection method\. This helps enforce hard constraints or local corrections\. The [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) manages the iteration of these projections through configurable [config\.py L392](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L392) and [config\.py L393](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L393)\.

 Finally, direct refinement on [config\.py L381](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L381) is performed, controlled by the [config\.py L382](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L382) parameter\. This involves iteratively refining the predicted [engine\.py L450](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L450) by performing gradient ascent on its log probability \(or, equivalently, gradient descent on its energy\)\. This refinement uses Monte\-Carlo sampling to estimate the log probability and its gradient, ensuring numerical stability\. The combined effects of these guidance, projection, and refinement steps allow the [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) to integrate differentiable geometric and chemical constraints directly into the generative process without requiring explicit model retraining\. For more details on how these potentials are configured, see [Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#training-free-guidance-tfg)\.### Differentiable Potentials and Constraint Enforcement

| Potential Name | Primary Purpose / Function | Notable Features / Methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| InterchainBondPotential | Enforces upper\-bound distance constraints for inter\-chain covalent bonds\. | Uses \_flat\_bottom\_linear for energy calculation\. |
| PairwiseDistancePotential | Applies lower/upper bounds to atom pairs, with category\-specific buffers and VDW corrections\. | Utilizes \_flat\_bottom\_parabolic and supports a \_project method for feasibility repair\. Includes caching for static per\-sample tensors and scale tables\. |
| StereoBondPotential | Enforces cis/trans stereochemistry for double bonds using absolute dihedral angles\. | Uses \_flat\_bottom\_linear for energy calculation based on \_abs\_dihedral\_value\_and\_grad\. |
| ChiralAtomPotential | Imposes chirality constraints on chiral centers using dihedral angles\. | Employs \_flat\_bottom\_linear for energy and features a \_project method with chain\-wise rescaling for feasibility\. |
| PlanarImproperPotential | Ensures planarity, typically for sp2 systems, using an improper torsion calculation\. | Calculates energy based on \_planar\_improper\_value\_and\_grad\. |
| LinearBondPotential | Enforces linearity, primarily for triple bonds, by constraining angles\. | Uses \_flat\_bottom\_linear to ensure angles are close to pi\. |
| ExperimentalTorsionPotential | Models torsion energy via a cosine\-series expansion\. | Energy calculation based on \_dihedral\_value\_and\_grad and a six\-term cosine series\. |
| VinaStericPotential | Implements a Vina\-style steric term for inter\-chain contacts\. | Identifies collision candidates across chains, applies an empirical potential \(two Gaussians \+ quadratic repulsion\), and uses caching for efficiency\. |

The [`protenix/tfg/potentials.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py) module defines a set of differentiable geometric and chemical constraints that are expressed as energy potentials\. These potentials operate on atomic coordinates, calculating penalty energies when constraints are violated and providing corresponding gradients and coordinate updates\. This functionality is central to the [Training\-Free Guidance \(TFG\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#training-free-guidance-tfg) engine, allowing it to steer the diffusion sampling process towards chemically and sterically plausible molecular structures\.

 All potentials inherit from a base [potentials\.py L68](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L68) class, which establishes a common interface for defining energy calculations and, optionally, coordinate projections\. Subclasses implement the [potentials\.py L90](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L90) method to compute energy and its gradient and can implement a [engine\.py L252](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L252) method to calculate coordinate updates\. These core methods are wrapped by public [config\.py L231](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L231), [config\.py L252](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L252), and [config\.py L276](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/config.py#L276) methods\. The framework internally employs the chain rule to translate gradients from geometric primitives \(like distances or angles\) back to atomic coordinates\.

 Key concrete implementations of potentials include:

 - [potentials\.py L594](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L594): This potential enforces distance bounds between general atom pairs\. It incorporates Van der Waals \(VDW\) radii to adjust these bounds and includes a projection method to correct feasibility violations\.
- [potentials\.py L849](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L849): This potential maintains the correct chirality of chiral centers by enforcing constraints on specific dihedral angles\. It also offers a projection method that can optionally rescale coordinates to preserve the molecule's radius of gyration\.
- [potentials\.py L984](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L984): This potential applies planarity constraints to molecular systems, particularly for sp2\-hybridized atoms, using improper dihedral angles to calculate energy and gradients\.
- [potentials\.py L1134](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L1134): This potential models inter\-chain steric interactions, drawing inspiration from the AutoDock Vina scoring function\. It identifies potential collision candidates across different chains and applies an empirical potential, comprising two Gaussians and a quadratic repulsion term, to penalize clashes\.

 Other potentials include [potentials\.py L553](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L553) for covalent bonds between chains, [potentials\.py L799](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L799) for cis/trans double bond constraints, [potentials\.py L1023](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L1023) for enforcing linearity, and [potentials\.py L1064](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L1064) for specific torsion energy calculations based on cosine series\. These potentials collectively provide the configurable energy terms that the [engine\.py L72](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/engine.py#L72) uses to guide the generation of biomolecular structures during inference\. The system also includes utilities for robust gradient aggregation \([potentials\.py L410](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L410)\) and iterative constraint projection \([potentials\.py L443](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/tfg/potentials.py#L443)\)\.## General Utilities and Helper Functions

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix leverages a comprehensive suite of general\-purpose utilities and helper functions to support various operations, from molecular data manipulation to distributed computing\. These utilities streamline common tasks, ensuring efficiency and consistency across the project\.

 For molecular data processing, Protenix includes functionalities for cropping [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) and [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) objects\. This involves identifying molecular types, finding interfacial tokens, and performing spatial or contiguous cropping as orchestrated by the [cropping\.py L413](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py#L413) class in [`protenix/utils/cropping.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py)\. This capability is essential for focusing computational efforts on relevant parts of large biomolecular assemblies\.

 The system also incorporates utilities for managing distributed computing environments\. The [distributed\.py L24](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L24) class and related functions such as [distributed\.py L33](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L33) and [distributed\.py L49](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L49) in [`protenix/utils/distributed.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py) facilitate the aggregation of metrics and ensure distributed\-aware operations across multiple processes\.

 File I/O operations are handled through various functions in [`protenix/utils/file_io.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/file_io.py), including efficient reading and caching of CSV, JSON, and LMDB files, as well as handling gzipped pickles and converting PDB to CIF formats\. This ensures robust and fast data access within the pipeline\.

 Geometric calculations, such as determining angles between 2D points and applying random 3D transformations to point sets, are provided by functions in [`protenix/utils/geometry.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/geometry.py)\. These are fundamental for structural manipulations and data augmentation\.

 For maintaining training stability and consistency, Protenix includes utilities for logging, learning rate scheduling, and random seed management\. The logging utility in [`protenix/utils/logger.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/logger.py) allows for configurable log levels and file output, with custom filtering for specific warnings\. Custom PyTorch learning rate schedulers, including [lr\_scheduler\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L22) and an [lr\_scheduler\.py L67](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L67), are implemented in [`protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py) to control learning dynamics\. Reproducibility across runs is ensured by the [seed\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/seed.py#L22) function in [`protenix/utils/seed.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/seed.py), which configures random number generation for various libraries, including PyTorch and NumPy\.

 Metric aggregation is managed by the [metrics\.py L30](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/metrics.py#L30) class in [`protenix/utils/metrics.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/metrics.py), which collects and calculates statistical metrics \(e\.g\., mean, median, percentiles\) across different namespaces, with optional distributed gathering\.

 PyTorch tensor operations are centralized in [`protenix/utils/torch_utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py), offering functions for device management, gradient norm calculation, conditional detachment, distance calculations, tensor manipulation, and parameter initialization using strategies like Glorot uniform\.

 A crucial aspect for accurate structural prediction and evaluation is the handling of symmetric permutation corrections\. The [permutation\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py#L22) class in [`protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py) orchestrates both atom\-level and chain\-level permutations, ensuring predicted structures are optimally aligned with ground\-truth labels by minimizing RMSD\. This is vital for symmetric molecules where identical atoms or chains can be swapped without altering chemical identity\. Atom\-level permutations are handled by [atom\_permutation\.py L272](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py#L272) in [`protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py), which optimizes permutations per residue by RMSD\. Chain\-level permutations, detailed in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation), can be either pocket\-based or a general heuristic, to align predicted chains to ground truth\. These utilities are critical for both training and inference stages to correctly evaluate and generate structures where symmetry might otherwise lead to misinterpretations of prediction quality\. For more details on this, see [Symmetric Permutation Correction for Molecular Structures](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#general-utilities-and-helper-functions-symmetric-permutation-correction-for-molecular-structures)\.

 Finally, the project includes specialized training utilities in [`protenix/utils/training.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/training.py), such as functions for creating AdamW and Adam optimizers, with support for weight decay and fine\-tuning, and a distributed\-aware mechanism for checking loss validity \(NaN/Inf\) during training\.### Molecular Data Cropping and Interface Identification

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix employs sophisticated mechanisms for cropping and identifying interfaces within molecular data, primarily to optimize computational efficiency and focus on regions of interest\. These operations are orchestrated by the [cropping\.py L413](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py#L413) class, which manages the manipulation of [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) and [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) objects\.

 The system can identify specific molecular types, such as metal atoms, within the structural data\. This is achieved by analyzing reference space unique identifiers, atom counts, chain IDs, and chain lengths, enabling the generation of masks and indices to pinpoint molecular entities in [`protenix/utils/cropping.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py)\.

 A key capability is the identification of interfacial tokens, which are crucial for understanding molecular interactions\. Protenix determines tokens that are in close contact with tokens from other chains based on a defined minimal distance\. By computing masks for tokens in different chains and combining them with distance\-based masks, the system can precisely locate these interfacial regions in [`protenix/utils/cropping.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py)\.

 For cropping structural data, Protenix supports both spatial and contiguous strategies:

 - **Spatial Cropping** selects a reference token and then identifies a specified number of nearest tokens around it\. This process can prioritize interfacial tokens if required\. Distance calculations are performed on token center atom coordinates, with tie\-breaking mechanisms to ensure deterministic selection in [`protenix/utils/cropping.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py)\.
- **Contiguous Cropping**, inspired by methods used in other protein structure prediction frameworks, involves shuffling chains and iteratively adding tokens until the desired crop size is reached\. This method can ensure that complete ligands or unstandardized residues are either fully included or excluded from the crop, preventing molecular fragmentation in [`protenix/utils/cropping.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py)\.

 The [cropping\.py L413](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py#L413) class in [`protenix/utils/cropping.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py) acts as the central control for these operations\. It initializes with parameters such as the target crop size, reference chain indices, and the [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) and [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) objects\. It then dynamically selects a cropping method based on predefined weights and prepares the necessary tensors from the [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) and [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) for cropping\. Once the target tokens are identified, [cropping\.py L413](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/cropping.py#L413) performs the physical crop by creating deep copies of the [tokenizer\.py L62](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/tokenizer.py#L62) and [dumper\.py L21](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/dumper.py#L21) and re\-indexing atomic information to reflect the new, cropped structure\. This meticulous handling of deep copies and re\-indexing ensures data integrity throughout the cropping process\.### Symmetric Permutation Correction for Molecular Structures

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Symmetric permutation correction addresses the ambiguity inherent in molecules with identical substructures or chains where the predicted structure might be chemically correct but topologically permuted relative to the ground truth\. This correction process is critical for accurate evaluation and generation of biomolecular structures, particularly in metrics like Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\), which are sensitive to atom and chain ordering\. Protenix employs a [permutation\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py#L22) handler, defined in [`protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py), to manage these corrections at both atom and chain levels, ensuring proper alignment during both training and inference\.

 The [permutation\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py#L22) class orchestrates the application of these corrections\. During training, it can permute ground\-truth labels to match predicted mini\-rollout structures\. For inference, it permutes predicted diffusion samples to align with ground\-truth labels\. This orchestration involves applying corrections to both atomic coordinates and various confidence metrics\.

 At the atomic level, the system, primarily through functionalities in [`protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py), identifies and corrects symmetric atoms within residues\. This is achieved by finding optimal atom permutations that minimize the RMSD between predicted and true coordinates\. The process often involves an initial global alignment to bring the overall structures into correspondence, followed by per\-residue optimization to address local symmetric ambiguities\.

 Chain\-level permutations, managed by the [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation) directory, can follow two main strategies\. For specific scenarios, such as protein\-ligand interactions, a pocket\-based permutation strategy \([pocket\_based\_permutation\.py L29](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/pocket_based_permutation.py#L29) in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/pocket_based_permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/pocket_based_permutation.py)\) is used\. This method focuses on optimizing chain assignments within the binding pocket to minimize ligand RMSD after aligning the pocket\. Alternatively, for general symmetric molecules, a heuristic approach \([heuristic\.py L42](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py#L42) in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py)\) is employed\. This heuristic, often anchor\-based, iteratively aligns a reference chain and then greedily matches remaining chains to find the optimal global chain assignment\.

 Both atom and chain permutation strategies rely on core utilities for calculating optimal transformations \([utils\.py L20](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py#L20) in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py)\) to align structures and apply these transformations \([utils\.py L58](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py#L58) in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py)\) to coordinates\. Robust error logging and debugging utilities, such as [utils\.py L110](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/utils.py#L110) in [`protenix/utils/permutation/utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/utils.py), are integrated to capture and diagnose issues that may arise during the complex permutation process\.#### Atom\-Level Symmetric Permutation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [atom\_permutation\.py L272](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py#L272) class in [`protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py) is designed to correct symmetric atoms within molecular residues\. This correction ensures that when comparing a predicted structure to a ground truth, ambiguities arising from chemically equivalent but positionally distinct atoms \(e\.g\., the hydrogens on a methyl group\) do not inflate Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\) values\. The process optimizes permutations at a per\-residue level, aiming to minimize the RMSD between predicted and true coordinates\.

 The permutation process begins by identifying residues that contain symmetric atoms\. Then, an initial global alignment of the predicted structure to the true structure is performed\. This step, handled by the [atom\_permutation\.py L314](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py#L314) method, ensures that subsequent per\-residue optimizations focus solely on local symmetric differences rather than overall structural misalignments\. Following this global alignment, the system systematically generates all possible permutations for the symmetric atoms within each residue\. By comparing the RMSD of the predicted residue against each of these permuted true residue configurations, the optimal permutation—the one yielding the lowest RMSD—is selected\. This allows for an accurate comparison of the local geometry of symmetric groups\.

 The [atom\_permutation\.py L200](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py#L200) function assists in preparing the data for this per\-residue optimization by batching permuted coordinates and masks, facilitating efficient computation\. The system is flexible, allowing either the true coordinates \([permutation\.py L66](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py#L66)\) or the predicted coordinates to be permuted to achieve the best alignment, depending on the specific evaluation context\. Error handling and detailed logging are integrated to monitor the permutation process and debug any issues, providing metrics such as [atom\_permutation\.py L634](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py#L634) and [atom\_permutation\.py L794](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/atom_permutation.py#L794) to quantify the improvement achieved by the symmetric correction\.#### Chain\-Level Symmetric Permutation Strategies

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix employs two primary strategies for correcting chain\-level symmetric permutations, which are crucial for accurately evaluating structural predictions where multiple chains may be chemically identical but predicted in a different order than the ground truth\. These strategies ensure that predicted structures are aligned optimally with reference structures, accounting for molecular symmetry\.

 The first strategy, *pocket\-based permutation*, is implemented in [pocket\_based\_permutation\.py L29](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/pocket_based_permutation.py#L29) within [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/pocket_based_permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/pocket_based_permutation.py)\. This approach specifically targets optimizing chain assignments within the context of a protein\-ligand binding pocket\. It is particularly useful for datasets where the interaction between a ligand and its surrounding protein chains is critical, such as in PoseBusters\. The method identifies candidate protein chains forming the pocket and candidate ligand chains\. It then iteratively aligns the predicted pocket to the true pocket, applies the resulting transformation to the entire predicted structure, and subsequently evaluates which predicted ligand chain best matches the true ligand chain based on minimizing the Root Mean Square Deviation \(RMSD\)\. This process helps to correctly assign chains that might be symmetric but have distinct roles in a binding interface\.

 The second strategy is a more general *heuristic approach* for symmetric molecules, managed by the [heuristic\.py L211](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py#L211) class in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py)\. This method, orchestrated by the [heuristic\.py L42](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/heuristic.py#L42) function, aims to find the optimal permutation of all chains in a predicted structure to match a symmetric ground truth\. It uses an "anchor\-based" algorithm: an anchor chain is selected from the predicted structure, and then iteratively aligned to potential anchor chains in the ground truth\. Once an initial alignment is established, the remaining chains are greedily matched based on their spatial proximity and similarity\. The algorithm prioritizes finding a match that minimizes the overall RMSD between the predicted and true structures, while also providing options to calculate RMSD based on chain centers for robustness\.

 Both permutation strategies utilize common geometric utilities for structural alignment\. The [utils\.py L20](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py#L20) function, defined in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py), calculates the optimal rotation and translation matrices required to align a source set of atomic coordinates to a target set, ensuring the alignment is free from reflections\. Once these transformation matrices are determined, the [utils\.py L58](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py#L58) function, also in [`protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/chain_permutation/utils.py), applies them to the predicted atomic coordinates, effectively rotating and translating the structure to minimize deviation from the ground truth\. These utilities are fundamental for repositioning molecular structures in 3D space to facilitate accurate comparison and permutation\.

 The overall management of these chain\-level permutations, alongside atom\-level permutations, is handled by the [permutation\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py#L22) class in [`protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/permutation/permutation.py)\. This class orchestrates when and how these permutation strategies are applied, distinguishing between needs during model training \(e\.g\., for mini\-rollout structures\) and inference \(for diffusion samples\), and ensuring consistent logging and error handling\. For more information on atom\-level permutation, refer to [Atom\-Level Symmetric Permutation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#general-utilities-and-helper-functions-symmetric-permutation-correction-for-molecular-structures-atom-level-symmetric-permutation)\.### Distributed Computing Utilities

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix incorporates utilities for managing operations within a distributed computing environment\. The [distributed\.py L24](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L24) class in [`protenix/utils/distributed.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py) initializes and stores information about the distributed setup, such as rank, world size, and node details, by reading environment variables\. This class provides the [distributed\.py L33](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L33) method, which can gather an object from all distributed processes, synchronizing data across the entire cluster\. This is particularly useful for collecting metrics\.

 To combine these gathered objects, the [distributed\.py L49](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L49) function merges lists of dictionaries into a single, comprehensive dictionary\. It can recursively process nested structures and apply an optional aggregation function to leaf values, which is key for consolidating metrics from multiple distributed processes\. These functionalities are brought together by [distributed\.py L68](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/distributed.py#L68), which orchestrates the collection and aggregation of metrics, ensuring that all processes contribute to a unified result\.### Custom Learning Rate Schedulers

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix incorporates several custom learning rate \(LR\) schedulers to manage the optimization process during model training, offering different strategies for adjusting the learning rate\. These schedulers, defined in [`protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py), extend PyTorch's [configs\_base\.py L89](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/configs/configs_base.py#L89) class and are designed to optimize convergence\.

 One such scheduler is [lr\_scheduler\.py L22](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L22), which first linearly increases the learning rate during a warmup phase and then gradually decreases it using a cosine annealing schedule\. This approach helps stabilize training at the beginning and allows for fine\-tuning towards the end\. Another is [lr\_scheduler\.py L67](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L67), which mimics the learning rate schedule observed in the AlphaFold3 model, characterized by an initial linear warmup followed by step\-wise exponential decay\. For scenarios requiring a fixed learning rate, [lr\_scheduler\.py L105](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L105) is available, maintaining the same learning rate throughout training\. Additionally, [lr\_scheduler\.py L116](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L116) is a composite scheduler that allows combining two distinct LR schedulers, useful for fine\-tuning specific parts of the model or training in stages\.

 The instantiation of these schedulers is centralized through the [lr\_scheduler\.py L147](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py#L147) function, also in [`protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/lr_scheduler.py)\. This factory function dynamically selects and configures the appropriate scheduler based on the provided training configuration, ensuring flexibility and ease of use in setting up diverse training regimes\. These custom schedulers contribute to the overall [Protenix Model Architecture and Training](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-model-architecture-and-training) by providing fine\-grained control over the optimization landscape\.### PyTorch Tensor Operations and Utilities

```
# Assuming 'model' is an nn.Module and 'optimizer' is an torch.optim.Optimizer
# and 'data' is a dict of tensors.
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

# Move data to the specified device
processed_data = to_device(data, device)

# Example usage of cdist for calculating Euclidean distances
tensor_a = torch.randn(10, 3)
tensor_b = torch.randn(5, 3)
distances = cdist(tensor_a, tensor_b)
# distances will have shape (10, 5)

# Example for calculating gradient norm
loss = model(processed_data).sum() # Stub: assume model and its forward pass
loss.backward()
total_grad_norm = grad_norm(model.parameters())
print(f"Total gradient norm: {total_grad_norm}")

# Detach a tensor if needed
original_tensor = torch.randn(2, 2, requires_grad=True)
detached_tensor = detach_if(original_tensor, detach=True)
# detached_tensor no longer tracks gradients
```

The collection of PyTorch utility functions within Protenix simplifies common operations related to tensor manipulation, device management, and gradient processing\. These utilities are centralized in [`protenix/utils/torch_utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py)\.

 Gradient norms can be calculated using the [torch\_utils\.py L24](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L24) function, which helps monitor the magnitude of gradients during model training\. Data movement between CPU and GPU devices is managed by the [torch\_utils\.py L35](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L35) function, ensuring tensors are on the correct hardware for computation\. For operations that require detaching tensors from the computation graph, [torch\_utils\.py L50](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L50) provides conditional detachment\.

 Distance calculations, specifically Euclidean distances, are handled by [torch\_utils\.py L56](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L56)\. This function can compute distances between two distinct tensor sets or within a single tensor\. Tensor dimensions can be reordered efficiently using [torch\_utils\.py L142](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L142)\. For scenarios requiring the flattening or unflattening of multiple tensors into a single contiguous block, [torch\_utils\.py L155](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L155) and [torch\_utils\.py L160](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L160) are available\.

 Parameter initialization is crucial for model stability and convergence\. [torch\_utils\.py L101](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L101) implements the Glorot \(Xavier\) uniform initialization for tensors, while [torch\_utils\.py L129](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/utils/torch_utils.py#L129) applies this strategy recursively to all parameters within a PyTorch module\.## Protenix Web Services

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protenix provides web service functionalities designed for computational biology inference, allowing integration into web\-based applications and offering interactive capabilities\. This service handles incoming requests, manages data and model downloads, performs Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) searches, and visualizes results\.

 The web service's core request processing logic resides in the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) class within [`protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py)\. This class is responsible for parsing incoming JSON requests, creating dedicated directories for each request, and managing the fetching of necessary common data files and specific model checkpoints from defined URLs\. It orchestrates the preparation of input data for the inference engine, including processing sequences and initiating MSA searches if required\. The [colab\_request\_parser\.py L137](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L137) method, in particular, constructs an input JSON dictionary, handles CCD \(Chemical Component Dictionary\) related file downloads, and validates the size of input complexes against predefined limits to prevent errors\. Once data is prepared, the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L463](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L463) method constructs and executes an external inference script to perform the actual prediction\.

 A key component of the web service is its interaction with the MMseqs2 service for MSA generation, detailed in [`protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py)\. The [colab\_request\_utils\.py L44](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py#L44) function manages submitting protein sequence queries to a remote MMseqs2 server, polling for job status, and downloading the alignment results\. This utility includes robust error handling with retries for network and server issues, ensuring reliable MSA generation\. It supports different server modes, such as "protenix" or "colabfold", which dictate the expected host URL and the post\-processing logic for the downloaded MSA files, indicating support for various backend configurations\. The [dependency\_url\.py L15](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py#L15) dictionary in [`protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py) centralizes the management of download URLs for various checkpoints and data files, including those required by the web service\.

 For analyzing and interpreting prediction results, [`protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py) offers tools for visualization\. It enables loading protein structure files and associated confidence data to generate 2D contact maps, visualize confidence metrics such as pLDDT, Predicted Distance Error \(PDE\), and Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE, as described in [Confidence Prediction and Score Calculation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-model-architecture-and-training-confidence-prediction-and-score-calculation)\), and create interactive 3D renderings of predicted protein structures using [requirements\.txt L13](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/requirements.txt#L13)\.

 The web service also provides interactive capabilities through [requirements\.txt L12](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/requirements.txt#L12) for defining complex molecular inputs, as implemented in [`protenix/web_service/viewer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py)\. Widgets such as [viewer\.py L20](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L20), [viewer\.py L174](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L174), and [viewer\.py L276](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L276) allow users to specify molecular sequences, modifications, and covalent bonds\. The [viewer\.py L429](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L429) integrates these widgets, enabling users to dynamically define complex molecular inputs and simulation parameters for the web service\. The [viewer\.py L133](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L133) method within [viewer\.py L429](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L429) collects, validates, and structures all user\-defined data into a comprehensive dictionary suitable as input for the molecular modeling application, ensuring data integrity\.### Web Service Request Processing and Inference Orchestration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The web service capabilities within Protenix enable the processing of biomolecular structure prediction requests through a [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) class, located in [`protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py)\. This class is responsible for receiving and interpreting incoming JSON requests\. For each request, the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) creates a dedicated directory for managing all associated files and outputs\.

 A key function of the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) is to orchestrate the download of necessary data and model files\. This involves fetching common data caches, such as chemical component dictionaries and protein cluster files, as well as specific model checkpoints required for the prediction task\. The paths for these resources are centrally managed within the [dependency\_url\.py L15](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py#L15) dictionary in [`protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py)\.

 The system also handles the crucial step of Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) searches\. If the request specifies [inference\_demo\.sh L32](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/inference_demo.sh#L32), the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) prepares the input sequences and initiates an MSA search\. The actual interaction with a remote MMseqs2 service for MSA generation is managed by the [colab\_request\_utils\.py L44](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py#L44) function in [`protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py)\. Following the search, the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) post\-processes the raw MSA results, which may involve splitting [colabfold\_msa\.py L220](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/scripts/colabfold_msa.py#L220) files into [msa\_search\.py L113](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L113) and [msa\_search\.py L114](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L114) based on sequence similarity and taxonomy, or generating dummy MSAs if no relevant alignments are found\.

 Once all data and MSAs are prepared and validated \(including checks for complex size limits that can trigger a [colab\_request\_parser\.py L68](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L68)\), the [colab\_request\_parser\.py L86](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_parser.py#L86) orchestrates the final execution of the inference pipeline\. This involves constructing and launching an external Python script, typically [`runner/inference.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py), which performs the actual structure prediction based on the prepared input and selected model\.### Interacting with the MMseqs2 Service for MSA Generation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [colab\_request\_utils\.py L44](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py#L44) function, found in [`protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py), manages the interaction with a remote MMseqs2 server to generate Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\)\. This process involves submitting protein sequence queries to the server, continuously checking the job's status, and then downloading and processing the results once the alignment is complete\. The function incorporates mechanisms for handling potential network or server errors through retries and manages authentication to the MMseqs2 service\.

 Queries can consist of either a single protein sequence or a list of sequences, and various parameters can be adjusted to control the MMseqs2 search, such as enabling environment searches, filtering, or template usage\. The [colab\_request\_utils\.py L56](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py#L56) parameter allows for different host URLs and post\-processing logic for the alignment results, adapting to different backend configurations \(e\.g\., "protenix" or "colabfold"\)\.

 The workflow begins with the submission of sequences to the MMseqs2 server\. If the server is busy or encounters a temporary issue, the system attempts to resubmit the query\. Following submission, the service periodically polls the server to monitor the job's progress\. Once the job status indicates completion, the results, typically in a [model\_1\.0\.0\_benchmark\.md?plain=1 L26](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/docs/model_1.0.0_benchmark.md?plain=1#L26) archive, are downloaded and extracted\.

 Depending on the [colab\_request\_utils\.py L56](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/colab_request_utils.py#L56), the extracted MSA files undergo specific processing\. For instance, in "protenix" mode, the system verifies the presence of expected alignment files\. In "colabfold" mode, the alignments may be further processed to generate [msa\_search\.py L114](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L114) or [msa\_search\.py L113](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/msa_search.py#L113) files, which are crucial for subsequent steps in the structure prediction pipeline\. The system also logs warnings and errors throughout this process to assist with debugging and monitoring\. For a broader understanding of how MSA generation fits into the overall data preparation workflow, refer to [Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) Data Generation and Featurization](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#data-management-and-preparation-for-protenix-multiple-sequence-alignment-msa-data-generation-and-featurization)\.### Managing Dependencies with Centralized URLs

```
URL = {
    # Checkpoint files for different Protenix models
    "protenix-v2": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/checkpoint/protenix-v2.pt",
    "protenix_base_default_v1.0.0": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/checkpoint/protenix_base_default_v1.0.0.pt",
    # ... other checkpoint URLs ...

    # Common data files
    "ccd_components_file": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/common/components.cif",
    "pdb_cluster_file": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/common/clusters-by-entity-40.txt",
    "obsolete_release_data_csv": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/common/obsolete_release_date.csv",
    # ... other common data URLs ...

    # Files used when template is enabled
    "obsolete_pdbs_path": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/common/obsolete_to_successor.json",
    "release_dates_path": "https://protenix.tos-cn-beijing.volces.com/common/release_date_cache.json",
}
```

The [dependency\_url\.py L15](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py#L15) dictionary, located in [`protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/dependency_url.py), centralizes the management of external resource locations for the Protenix web service\. This dictionary maps descriptive keys to HTTPS URLs, facilitating the organized retrieval of various essential assets such as model checkpoints and common data files\. For instance, it specifies download paths for [inference\.py L300](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L300), [inference\.py L302](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L302), and [inference\.py L303](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/runner/inference.py#L303), which are crucial for data processing and model inference\. The structured approach of this dictionary ensures that all necessary dependencies are easily identified and managed, supporting the web service's operational needs\. This centralized approach simplifies updates and maintenance, as all external URLs are stored in a single, accessible location\. Further details on how these dependencies are utilized can be found in [Web Service Request Processing and Inference Orchestration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-web-services-web-service-request-processing-and-inference-orchestration)\.### Prediction Visualization for Analysis and Interpretation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Prediction visualization within Protenix offers tools to interpret and analyze the results of biomolecular structure predictions\. This functionality is primarily handled by [`protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py) in the [`protenix/web_service`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service) directory, enabling users to generate visual representations of predicted structures and associated confidence metrics\.

 The [prediction\_visualization\.py L30](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py#L30) class provides the capability to load both the predicted protein structures, stored in CIF format \([utils\.py L754](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/data/utils.py#L754)\), and their corresponding confidence data, typically in JSON format\. Once loaded, various visualization methods become available\. For example, two\-dimensional contact maps can be generated to illustrate inter\-residue distances within the predicted structures using [prediction\_visualization\.py L91](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py#L91)\.

 Confidence measures are also visualized to provide insights into the reliability of different parts of the prediction\. This includes plotting metrics such as pLDDT \(predicted Local Distance Difference Test\) scores, which indicate per\-residue confidence, as well as Predicted Aligned Error \(PAE\) and Predicted Distance Error \(PDE\) heatmaps, which show the expected error in relative positions between residues\. These plots, generated by [prediction\_visualization\.py L128](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py#L128), can incorporate global confidence metrics like pLDDT, global PDE \(gPDE\), PTM \(predicted TM\-score\), and iPTM \(interface predicted TM\-score\)\.

 For a more immersive analysis, interactive three\-dimensional renderings of the predicted protein structures can be generated using [requirements\.txt L13](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/requirements.txt#L13) through the [prediction\_visualization\.py L210](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/prediction_visualization.py#L210) function\. These 3D visualizations can be colored according to pLDDT scores, providing an intuitive way to identify regions of high or low confidence directly on the molecular model\. The visualization tools also support options for displaying sidechains and mainchains, allowing for detailed inspection of specific structural features\.

 The overall framework supports the systematic loading and plotting of prediction results, particularly for individual "best sample" predictions, facilitating a comprehensive assessment of the model's output\. Further details on how these web services handle requests and manage dependencies can be found in [Web Service Request Processing and Inference Orchestration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-web-services-web-service-request-processing-and-inference-orchestration) and [Managing Dependencies with Centralized URLs](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-web-services-managing-dependencies-with-centralized-urls)\.### Interactive Input Definition with Jupyter Widgets

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [requirements\.txt L12](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/requirements.txt#L12) in [`protenix/web_service/viewer.py`](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py) enable users to interactively define complex molecular inputs and simulation parameters, which are subsequently used by the web service for tasks such as biomolecular structure prediction\. These widgets facilitate the construction of diverse molecular systems directly within a Jupyter environment\.

 Entities within a molecular complex, such as DNA, RNA, proteins, ligands, and ions, can be defined using specialized widgets\. For instance, [viewer\.py L20](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L20) allows users to specify sequences, copy numbers, and post\-translational modifications for DNA, RNA, or protein components\. Ligands can be introduced via their SMILES strings using [viewer\.py L174](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L174) or by their Chemical Component Dictionary \(CCD\) codes through [viewer\.py L217](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L217), which also supports ion definitions\.

 Beyond individual molecular components, the [viewer\.py L276](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L276) provides an interface to define covalent linkages between different entities, specifying the involved atoms and their positions\. Simulation parameters for the underlying molecular modeling application are configured using the [viewer\.py L372](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L372), where users can set diffusion model parameters like sample counts, steps, cycles, and random seeds, as well as select a model version\.

 All these individual entity and parameter widgets are integrated into a single, comprehensive [viewer\.py L429](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L429)\. This main viewer allows users to dynamically add, remove, and configure various molecular entities, alongside global settings such as whether to use Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) or atom confidence\. The [viewer\.py L429](https://github.com/bytedance/protenix/blob/c3bfc365b3e1341a11935eddfe7bfdc308092147/protenix/web_service/viewer.py#L429) also validates the user\-defined data, ensuring its integrity before structuring it into a dictionary format suitable for the molecular modeling pipeline\. This interactive approach streamlines the process of preparing complex inputs for the Protenix web service, as discussed in [Protenix Web Services](https://codewiki.google/github.com/bytedance/protenix#protenix-web-services)\.
